about: Per-task labels of the ARC-AGI-2 pool (the 114 evaluation tasks new to the edition): the symmetries of the square under which each task's rule is unchanged, and the colours with a fixed role in it, which are never relabelled (colour 0 is always fixed). The track draws each task's augmentation only from these (Dan, 26 Sep 2026).
method: Two independent labelling passes by an AI assistant over images and grids of every pair; merged conservatively: a symmetry only if both passes allow it (then the largest subgroup of D8 inside that), a colour fixed if either pass fixes it, and identity with every used colour fixed where either pass did not understand the rule or was not confident. Symmetry names follow continual_arc.augment.SYMMETRY_NAMES.

135a2760.rule: Each framed strip holds a periodic motif with a few defective cells; repair the defects so the motif repeats exactly along the whole strip (frames and background unchanged).

13e47133.rule: Walls divide the grid into regions; in each region the colours placed diagonally from one of its corners (the corner cell up to the last non-background diagonal cell) are repeated as concentric rings, each cell taking colour number (Chebyshev distance to the region's boundary) mod sequence length; regions without seeds stay unchanged.

142ca369.rule: Every L-tromino fires a diagonal ray from its corner cell, pointing away from its missing corner; the ray bounces off any object it meets (reversing the component of motion that points at the object) and from the bounce on takes that object's colour, until it leaves the grid.

16de56c4.rule: All the pattern lines start at the same grid edge; in each line perpendicular to that edge, the first two same-coloured cells from the edge fix a period, and that colour is repeated at the period along the line; if a differently coloured cell lies exactly on the progression, the progression stops there and all of it takes that cell's colour, otherwise it runs to the far edge and off-progression cells are left alone.

1818057f.rule: Every plus shape (a cell and its four orthogonal neighbours) made entirely of yellow on the red background is recoloured light blue; all other cells are unchanged.

195c6913.rule: The row of 2x2 blocks in the top-left gives a colour sequence and the lone 2x2 block elsewhere gives an end colour; from each single-cell marker on the left edge draw a path that goes right until the next cell leaves the marker's region, paints that blocking cell with the end colour, turns up, and so on alternating right and up (a staircase toward the top right), colouring the path with the sequence cyclically; the path stops at the grid edge or when its new direction is blocked at once; the legend and the end block are erased.

1ae2feb7.rule: A full-length wall line has bars of coloured segments touching it on one side; each bar is continued on the other side of the wall, where a segment of length L paints its colour every L cells counting from the wall, and segments nearer the wall paint over farther ones.

20270e3b.rule: Two yellow pieces carry orange marker cells; translate one piece so that each piece's orange cells fall on yellow cells of the other (the pieces interlock), merge them with orange turned yellow, and output the bounding box of the combined shape on the blue background.

20a9e565.rule: The shapes form a sequence that grows step by step with cycling colours (longer E shapes, taller ladders, wider waves, longer chevron strips, a growing staircase of arches); two grey L-shaped corner marks outline a window; output the window's contents after the sequence is continued into it.

21897d95.rule: Each blue T-marker (three blue cells around a centre cell) points its nub into a neighbouring region, and that whole region takes the marker's colour (the centre's colour if it is not blue, otherwise the colour of the region the marker sits in); markers are erased. If a maroon 5-cell L is present it is erased too, and the grid is rotated a quarter turn: counter-clockwise when the L's horizontal arm runs left from its corner (a top-right corner), clockwise when it runs right (a top-left corner).

221dfab4.rule: A yellow bar on one edge defines a stripe across the grid, as wide as the bar; counting lines outward from the bar, the stripe is painted yellow at even distances except every third even line (distance 4, 10, 16...), where the stripe and every object cell on that whole line turn green; at odd distances the stripe is cleared to background.

247ef758.rule: Each small shape left of the separator whose colour appears on the box border is moved into the box, centred where the row marked by its colour on the side border meets the column marked on the top border, with one copy for every marked row and column; shapes whose colour is not marked stay put; where copies overlap, shapes that stood higher in the left panel are drawn on top.

269e22fb.rule: Every input is a crop of one fixed 20x20 two-colour picture (the one shown in the demo outputs), in some orientation and with some pair of colours; output the whole picture in the crop's orientation and colours.

271d71e2.rule: Each black-framed box slides toward the maroon bars on one side, pushing the adjacent bar ahead of it, one cell per grey interior cell, stopping early when the pushed bar would reach the next bar; each step turns one grey interior cell orange, filling line by line from the leading side, and within each line in the direction of the motion turned 90 degrees clockwise.

28a6681f.rule: Blue behaves as a liquid under gravity: keeping the number of blue cells fixed, the blue falls downward, runs along the tops of the other shapes and over their edges, and pools from the bottom up in the basins it reaches (grid edges act as walls).

291dc1e1.rule: The 0 corner cell has a blue line along one edge and a red line along the other; objects lie in two-cell-thick lanes parallel to the blue line; read the lanes starting from the blue line and, within each lane, from the red end; output the objects stacked top to bottom in that order, each turned so that its red-side end is on the left (lanes horizontal), centred on a light-blue background as wide as the longest object.

2b83f449.rule: Every orange 777 in a black row becomes 868 and the cells directly above and below its centre turn magenta (a vertical magenta bar). Each green end marker of a light-blue row then rolls inward: if the first bar it meets leads down from its row, it drops through to the next light-blue row and rolls on in the opposite direction, repeating, until it reaches the end of a light-blue segment (grid edge or black gap), where it stops; if the first bar it meets comes down from above, or its segment has no bar, it stays. Markers ending at the same place stack inward.

2ba387bc.rule: The grid holds 4x4 squares, some hollow and some solid; output a two-column grid with the hollow squares stacked in the left column and the solid squares in the right column, each column ordered by the squares' vertical position in the input (top first), the shorter column padded with black 4x4 blocks at the bottom.

2c181942.rule: A small ring in the middle has four coloured sides; every loose shape whose colour matches a side is moved to that side and turned so that its two-cell connector touches the side, centred on it, with the rest of the shape pointing outward; loose shapes matching no side are erased.

2d0172a1.rule: Redraw the hand-drawn picture as a tidy schematic: each closed loop becomes a rectangular frame and each blob a single cell, keeping which elements lie inside which and their relative arrangement (left/right/above/below), with one background cell between neighbouring elements, cropped to the schematic.

31f7f899.rule: Vertical bars of various colours cross a horizontal magenta line; keep each bar's colour and column but reassign the bar lengths (vertical extents) so that they increase from left to right.

332f06d7.rule: A black square and a red square of the same size sit at the ends of a blue corridor on green; the black square slides along the corridor toward the red one as far as a square of its size fits, taking the red square's place if it gets there; its old position becomes blue.

35ab12c3.rule: Points of the same colour are joined into a polyline or closed polygon with horizontal, vertical or 45-degree segments (points that cannot be joined this way stay as they are); a single point of another colour touching one of a shape's points marks a copy of that shape shifted by the offset between the two points, drawn beneath the original.

36a08778.rule: Magenta streams run down from the top; when a stream reaches a red horizontal bar it wraps around it (a magenta row just above the bar, one cell wider than the bar at each end) and continues down both sides; streams run to the bottom edge.

38007db0.rule: A grid of framed panels; in each row of panels all panels show the same small pattern except one; output a single column of panels, one per row, showing that row's odd one out.

3a25b0d8.rule: There are two figures with the same topology: one outline-only template and one whose enclosed compartments are coloured; output the template, cropped, with each compartment filled with the colour of the corresponding compartment in the coloured figure.

3dc255db.rule: Each open shape (a cup, arch, bracket or chevron) holds a few cells of another colour inside its opening; remove them and draw that many cells of their colour as a straight line sticking out from the shape's closed end (its apex), directly away from the opening, cut off at the grid edge.

3e6067c3.rule: Framed boxes each hold a coloured centre; the row of single coloured cells (the legend) gives an order read left to right; join the boxes in that order with bridges across the gaps between consecutive (adjacent) boxes, each bridge as wide as the centre patch and coloured with the colour of the box it leaves.

409aa875.rule: Each small three-cell chevron points away from its open side (up, down, left or diagonally); mark the cell five steps beyond its tip in that direction maroon; if the mark falls on another chevron, that whole chevron turns maroon; if two marks fall on the same cell, it turns blue.

446ef5d2.rule: Fragments of one framed rectangle are scattered; assemble them into the complete rectangle without rotating them, keeping in place the fragment marked by a small L-shaped marker (the marker's missing corner is the rectangle's corner), and remove the marker.

45a5af55.rule: The input is a stack of uniform horizontal stripes; output concentric square rings of side 2*(rows-1), the top row as the outermost ring and each following row one ring further in, so the last rows form the centre.

4a21e3da.rule: A red cell on the grid edge marks a cutting line across the grid (two red cells mark two lines); the orange shape is cut along the line(s) and each part is pushed into the corner on its side, toward the marker's edge; the line is drawn in red from the marker to the far end of the shape's extent, and the shape's own cells on the line stay orange.

4c3d4a41.rule: The grey comb (a base with teeth) on the left slides into the box on the right, base at the bottom and teeth under the coloured columns; each tooth pushes the stack of cells in its column upward until the stack rests on it, and whatever is pushed past the top row is lost.

4c416de3.rule: Black rectangular frames have coloured marker cells just inside some corners, and one corner in the input already shows a complete decoration; give every marked corner the same decoration in its marker's colour, mirrored to fit that corner.

4c7dc4dd.rule: Two large frames each hold two small boxes: in one frame both boxes are filled and show a change (complement; a path drawn between marker cells; a plus turned into a ring; a corner seed completed into a full pattern), in the other one box is filled and one is empty; output the empty box's contents, the same change applied to the filled box in its own colours.

4e34c42c.rule: Several pieces share identical edge sections; overlap the matching sections (without rotating any piece) to join the pieces into one picture, and output that picture cropped.

53fb4810.rule: Blue blobs carry short coloured stubs, and one blob already shows its stub extended as a full ray to the grid edge; extend every other stub outward from its blob to the grid edge, repeating the stub's pattern and drawing over anything it crosses.

5545f144.rule: The panels (one or more, separated by lines) are successive frames of a shape travelling along a chain of dots, each dot in line with the last, consuming each dot it reaches and turning to face its direction of travel; output one panel with the shape at the end of the chain, facing the direction of its last move, and no dots left.

581f7754.rule: Each lone marker cell on the grid border defines a line (its row if it sits on the left/right border, its column if on the top/bottom border); every object containing a cell of that marker's colour (including lone cells of that colour) slides parallel to that border until its marker-coloured cell lies on that line; nothing else changes.

58490d8a.rule: The output is the black panel: for each legend colour in the panel's left column, count the separate shapes of that colour in the picture and draw that many cells of that colour in the legend's row, every other cell, starting at the legend cell and going right.

58f5dbd5.rule: Crop to the block of solid 5x5 squares with their one-cell margin; into each square's 3x3 centre cut the small 3x3 shape of the same colour as background-coloured holes (shape cells become background, the other centre cells keep the square's colour); small shapes with no matching square are dropped.

5961cc34.rule: The red bar fires a red beam from its yellow tip, in the direction the tip points, straight to the grid edge; every blue blob the beam hits turns red and sends the beam on out of its green-marked side (beam as wide as the green mark); blobs not hit are erased, and the tip and green marks become part of the red path.

5dbc8537.rule: The grid has a silhouette half (a frame colour with holes in the other half's background colour) and a pieces half; output the silhouette half with its holes exactly tiled by all the coloured pieces, each placed unrotated where it fits.

62593bfd.rule: Objects that have a twin (another object of the same shape up to rotation/reflection) slide straight up until they touch the top edge; objects without a twin slide straight down until they touch the bottom edge; columns do not change.

64efde09.rule: Several identical two-line bars (a plain line beside a patterned strip) lie in different orientations; each lone coloured cell on the grid border lines up with one position along a bar facing that border; every bar then shoots a line of that colour, from the same position along its length, out of its plain side to the grid edge.

65b59efc.rule: Grey lines split the input into a top row of NxN patterns (one colour each), a middle row whose cells, overlaid, give an NxN layout in those colours, and a bottom row with a new colour under each pattern; output an N^2 x N^2 grid with, at every layout cell, the pattern of that colour drawn in its new colour.

67e490f4.rule: Output the big template pattern, filling each of its holes with the colour that occurs most often among the scattered small shapes having the same shape as that hole (up to rotation).

6e453dd6.rule: Slide every black shape toward the grey line until it touches it; then, for each row in which the shape touches the line and has an enclosed background hole, colour the cells on the far side of the grey line red.

6e4f6532.rule: Each light-blue object with a maroon core and coloured tips is moved, rotated or mirrored as needed, so that its maroon cells cover the lone maroon mark of the same shape and every coloured tip points at the border or wall of the same colour.

6ffbe589.rule: Crop the large concentric object; rotate each of its colour layers clockwise about the centre by 90 degrees times the number of cells in the small stray piece of that colour elsewhere in the grid (a layer with no stray piece stays as it is).

71e489b6.rule: In the blue/black picture, every small black speck inside or notched into a blue area gets an orange ring on all eight neighbours, and every small blue speck in a black area is erased to black.

7491f3cf.rule: The strip holds four panels: panel 1 has a line splitting the square in two with an extra mark in one part; fill the empty panel 4 with panel 2's pattern in the marked part and panel 3's pattern in the other part, overlaying both on the line itself (panel 2 on top).

7666fa5d.rule: Fill red every background cell that lies between two parallel diagonal line segments, i.e. on a perpendicular diagonal between two segments and within the span of both.

78332cb0.rule: Rearrange the 5x5 panels into a single line with magenta separators, ordered so that the shapes join across the separators into one continuous path; the line runs vertically if the shapes join top-to-bottom and horizontally if they join left-to-right.

7b0280bc.rule: In the graph of nodes joined by line paths, find the route between the two special-colour nodes that passes through the fewest ordinary nodes; recolour that route's lines grey (5) and its ordinary nodes green (3).

7b3084d4.rule: Fit the four coloured pieces together, rotating them as needed, into a solid square in which the piece holding the grey cell is placed so that the grey cell is in the top-left corner; output that square.

7b5033c1.rule: Follow the single path of coloured segments from its top end to its other end and output the colours of its cells, in that order, as one column (N x 1).

7b80bb43.rule: Delete every stray diagonal segment; where a diagonal segment branched off the end of a straight line next to a gap in that line, fill the gap so the line is continuous again (gaps without such a branch stay open).

7c66cb00.rule: Each colour part of every small object at the top drops into the band whose fill colour equals that part's colour, keeping its columns and shape, lands on the bottom of that band and is drawn in the band's end-cap colour; the top area is cleared.

7ed72f31.rule: Every object touching a red element gets a mirrored copy added: reflected across the red line if the element is a line, or rotated 180 degrees about the red cell if it is a single cell; originals stay.

800d221b.rule: A network of line-coloured paths joins a central 3x3 hub to several patterned end regions; each path, together with the line-coloured border of its end region, takes that region's majority colour; the hub's ring keeps the line colour and its centre takes the colour held by most of the paths leaving the hub.

80a900e0.rule: On the blue/black checkerboard, each diamond has coloured diagonal edge segments; from both end cells of every coloured edge, draw a diagonal ray of that colour outward (perpendicular to the edge, away from the diamond) to the grid edge.

8698868d.rule: Each big tile carries some dots of the background colour; put into each tile, centred with a one-cell margin, the small shape whose number of holes equals the tile's number of dots (holes showing the tile colour, dots removed), and output just the block of tiles.

88bcf3b4.rule: A tail hangs off one end of a straight anchor line; redraw it from the same attachment cell with the same length as a path that heads diagonally to the nearby target object, wraps tightly around the target's far side and then runs on diagonally (cut off at the grid edge); the old tail is erased.
88bcf3b4.merge: not understood or low confidence in a pass: identity, every used colour fixed

88e364bc.rule: Each outline shape has a key panel with a border of the same colour containing an arrow with a red head; every yellow dot inside that outline slides in the arrow's direction (straight or diagonal) until it touches the outline.

89565ca0.rule: Count the compartments of each coloured rectangle outline; output one row per outline, sorted from fewest compartments (top) to most, with that many cells of the outline's colour from the left and the rest of the row, up to the widest count, in the noise colour.

898e7135.rule: The big shape with holes becomes the output canvas, scaled by the size factor of the small shapes; each hole is filled with the colour of the small shape of the same form (up to rotation/reflection); noise dots are dropped.

8b7bacbf.rule: Coloured cells at the ends of line paths are markers; every closed loop connected through the path network to a marker has its enclosed hole filled with that marker's colour; loops in networks with no marker are left alone.

8b9c3697.rule: A red block that matches a comb's notch in size and lines up with it slides into the notch, and the cells it travelled over become black (0); red blocks that fit no notch are erased.

8e5c0c38.rule: Make every object mirror-symmetric left-to-right about its best vertical axis by deleting the cells that have no mirror partner.

8f215267.rule: For each hollow frame, count the scattered small shapes of the frame's colour and draw that many single cells of that colour on the frame's middle row, every other cell starting from the right end; erase all the scattered shapes.

8f3a5a89.rule: In the light-blue region containing the magenta corner cell, every cell touching (8-neighbours) the grid border or a blue wall connected to the border becomes orange; blue shapes outside that region are erased (a blue island inside it stays and is not outlined).

9385bd28.rule: The two-column key in the bottom-left pairs a colour (left) with a fill colour (right); taking pairs top to bottom, the box spanned by the two corner pieces of the left colour is painted with the right colour on every cell not claimed by an earlier pair, keeping its own corner pieces (fill 0 claims the box without painting); a left colour that appears as one solid 2x2 block is simply recoloured.

97d7923e.rule: Short vertical key bars hang from the top-left; a key bar of colour C and length n means the n-th tallest standing column capped with C has its middle recoloured to C.

9aaea919.rule: Stacks of plus-shaped blocks stand on the bottom; stacks above a red bar turn grey; the stack above the green bar grows upward by as many blocks as the red-marked stacks hold in total; the bars are erased.

9bbf930d.rule: Orange corridors between two parallel walls of the same colour act as pipes: from each magenta border cell whose row is such a corridor, the magenta turns orange and the flow follows the corridor (round turns and into further same-colour corridors), then runs straight on; a magenta cell is put where the flow stops (at the grid edge, or just before an obstacle).
9bbf930d.merge: not understood or low confidence in a pass: identity, every used colour fixed

a251c730.rule: Two framed rectangles sit on a striped background: one holds complete stamps (a small shape with one differently coloured marker cell), the other holds only lone marker cells. Output the second rectangle with its frame, drawing the matching stamp around each lone marker so the marker cells coincide.

a25697e4.rule: Each two-coloured piece is moved (translated, rotated or reflected as needed) so that one of its colour parts exactly fills the notch of a socket shape standing at a grid edge; if the fit needs a reflection, the piece's two colours are swapped (the part in the notch takes the other part's colour).

a32d8b75.rule: The main area is flanked by magenta-separated side panel(s), each holding a two-colour tile, a shape and a key: a box with a yellow dot marking a corner and a box with an orange arrow from its centre. Rotate the shape so its top points where the arrow points, scale it by the tile size, anchor it at the marked corner of the main area and stamp the tile with its two colours swapped at each shape cell; output the main area.

a395ee82.rule: A solid shape and a sparse dot pattern (dots two apart, two colours) are given; the dot of the shape's colour marks the shape's position. Scale the dot pattern up by the shape size so each dot becomes a copy of the shape, aligned so the marked dot's copy is the original shape; copies take the swapped colour (dots of the other colour give copies in the shape colour, the marked copy takes the other colour); dots are erased.

a47bf94d.rule: Light-blue pipes (grey cells mark where one pipe passes under another; maroon blocks are tunnels pipes pass straight through) join pairs of end slots. Turn each solid 3x3 square into a diamond outline of its colour and draw an X of that colour at the other end of its pipe; an existing X gets a diamond of its colour at its pipe's other end.

a6f40cea.rule: Output the interior of the green-bordered rectangle, showing the parts of the other rectangular outlines that pass behind it, each continued with its own pattern (solid, or alternating two colours). ANOMALY: in demo 3 the hidden part of the maroon/light-blue outline has the opposite alternation phase to its visible part, while the yellow/grey outline in the same demo and the maroon/yellow outline in the test keep the phase; no single rule reproduces all outputs (likely a data error).
a6f40cea.merge: not understood or low confidence in a pass: identity, every used colour fixed

abc82100.rule: Each key is a straight line: colour A, colour B, then a light-blue stamp, the dot-position being the cell just after B. Erase the keys and replace every cell of colour A with the stamp drawn in colour B, positioned (same orientation) so the dot-position lands on that cell; colours without a key stay.

b0039139.rule: Blue lines split the input into four panels: a yellow motif, green marks, and two solid colour panels. Output the motif repeated N times (N = number of green marks) along the panels' axis with one-cell separators, motif cells in the colour of the solid panel next to the green panel and everything else in the colour of the outer solid panel.

b10624e5.rule: A blue cross splits the grid into quadrants; one quadrant holds a template (a red square with coloured blocks attached). In every other quadrant attach the same blocks around its red square, scaled by the ratio of square sizes and mirrored across the blue line(s) separating it from the template quadrant (clipped at the edge).

b5ca7ac4.rule: Framed 5x5 squares slide horizontally: light-blue-framed squares slide to the left edge and red-framed squares to the right edge, each stopping against the edge or a square already moved the same way in overlapping rows.

b6f77b65.rule: The colour(s) of the corner cell(s) at the top-left name pieces to delete from a stack of arches (legs and lintels); after deleting them everything settles under gravity: legs drop until resting on something, lintels drop until held by legs at both ends or resting on something. ANOMALY: demo 2's output has one extra red cell at (4,5) (red count 7 to 8), which no settling rule produces (likely a data error).
b6f77b65.merge: not understood or low confidence in a pass: identity, every used colour fixed

b99e7126.rule: A lattice of identical 3x3 tiles contains a few copies of a special tile; the cells of the special tile's new colour form a 3x3 shape. Add special tiles so that the special tiles, at tile scale, form that same shape (completing the partial shape).

b9e38dc0.rule: A container outline has an opening and a seed colour inside. Fill the container with the seed colour and let it pour out of the opening, spreading between the continuations of the container's walls (same slope) to the grid edge; any other cell in the way leaves a straight shadow behind it in the flow direction.

bf45cf4b.rule: Replace each cell of the single-colour shape with a copy of the multi-colour tile, and each empty cell of its bounding box with background, giving a grid of (shape size x tile size).

c4d067a0.rule: A small key of single-cell dots (two apart) is a map; a few big blocks form an enlarged copy of part of it. Draw the rest of the enlarged key with the blocks' size and spacing, aligned so the existing blocks sit on the unique place in the key they match.

c7f57c3e.rule: Objects share one blue frame shape (at different scales) and come in two variants distinguished by their coloured parts; each object is switched to the other variant (its coloured parts replaced by the other variant's, scaled to its size).

cb2d8a2c.rule: A green path starts at the green border cell and crosses the grid, detouring around each red bar attached to a border while keeping a clearance equal to the number of blue cells in that bar, and exits at the opposite border; the bars become solid red.

cbebaa4b.rule: Assemble the jigsaw: the yellow piece stays put and every other piece is translated so its red connector dots coincide with matching red dots on the assembled structure, forming one connected figure.

d35bdbdc.rule: 3x3 blocks (frame colour plus centre colour) are linked by a grey path. Keep the two blocks at the ends of the path and erase all others; each kept block's centre becomes the centre colour of the block whose frame colour equals the kept block's old centre colour.

d59b0160.rule: A green-fenced 3x3 key in a corner lists colours. Erase (to the orange background) every black box that contains every key colour; keep all other boxes.

d8e07eb2.rule: A header shows 3-4 symbols from the fixed 4x4 symbol table below the magenta line. Box each of those symbols in the table in green (adjacent boxes merge); if they make up a whole row or column, the header and footer backgrounds turn green, otherwise the footer turns red.

db0c5428.rule: A 9x9 ring of 3x3 blocks around a hollow centre is expanded to a 5x5 block layout: the original stays, each outer block is copied unchanged to the opposite side of the centre at twice its distance, and the centre is filled with a 3x3 shrink of the ring of cells around the hole (its corners and edge-midpoints to the 3x3 ring, the remaining colour to the middle).

db695cfb.rule: Join each two blue cells that lie on a common diagonal with a blue diagonal line; every magenta cell on such a line sends a magenta diagonal line perpendicular to it across the whole grid.

dbff022c.rule: A two-cell-wide key along a grid edge lists colour pairs; the cell on the edge side names a shape colour and the inner cell its fill colour. Fill the enclosed holes of each hollow shape with the fill colour paired with its colour; shapes whose colour is not an edge-side key colour stay unchanged.

dd6b8c4b.rule: Maroon cells that can reach the central 3x3 green square without crossing magenta walls move into it: the nearest (by path length) first, at most nine, filling the square in reading order (the red centre counts as a cell), and they vanish from where they were.

de809cff.rule: Two overlapping colour regions contain black holes. Turn every hole light blue and surround it with a 3x3 ring of the other region's colour; clean up strays (other-colour cells inside a region take the region colour, stray cells outside the regions are erased).

dfadab01.rule: Each marker colour stands for a 4x4 pattern (red: yellow hollow square; green: blue ring; grey: magenta double-diagonal blocks; light blue: orange X). Replace every marker by its pattern with the marker at the pattern's top-left corner; erase the legend (a drawn pattern with its marker just beyond its bottom-right corner) and everything else.

e12f9a14.rule: Each object is a 2x2 coloured core inside a 4x4 ring with gaps; from every gap a ray of the core colour runs outward (straight from an edge gap, diagonal from a corner gap) to the border, and rays that meet both bend to the average of their directions and run on side by side. ANOMALY: in demo 3 the yellow object's bottom-right corner gap emits no ray although identical corner gaps emit rays everywhere else (likely a data error).
e12f9a14.merge: not understood or low confidence in a pass: identity, every used colour fixed

e3721c99.rule: A legend panel, cut off from the work area by a blue line, holds template blocks of different colours with 0, 1, 2, ... enclosed holes; every grey shape in the work area is recoloured with the colour of the template that has the same number of holes, and grey shapes whose hole count matches no template are erased.

e376de54.rule: The grid holds several parallel straight segments (all horizontal, all vertical or all diagonal) whose starting ends lie on a common perpendicular line; every segment is extended or trimmed at its free end so that it has the length of the middle segment of the set, each keeping its colour.

e8686506.rule: The largest object (it may be made of two colours) is a frame whose bounding box contains background holes; every other small object is a piece that exactly fills one of those holes in its given orientation; the output is the frame's bounding box with each piece set into the hole it fits.

e87109e9.rule: The top band is a legend of four grey-framed boxes, each showing one colour on its left or right side; the light-blue square in the main area sends beams of its own width in all four directions, each running straight until it meets a coloured block, where it turns left if that colour is on the left of its legend box and right if on the right, and continuing until it leaves the grid; the output is the main area (legend removed) with the beams drawn in light blue.

edb79dae.rule: Outside a grey frame there are legend keys, each a small block whose left colour A juts into its right colour B, giving mappings A -> B, and one pattern shape drawn in each source colour A; the output is the grey-framed region in which every solid block of colour A is replaced by A's pattern drawn in colour B on the background.

eee78d87.rule: The 6x6 orange input contains one 3x3 shape; the output is 16x16, with the shape drawn in black on orange centred on every point (3i, 3j) for i, j = 0..5 (the shape tiled with period 3), after which every black cell inside the central 6x6 square (rows and columns 5-10) becomes maroon.

f560132c.rule: One of four shapes contains a 2x2 colour key; that shape (key cells counted as part of it) stays unrotated in the top-left corner while the other three shapes are rotated to complete a solid square with it; each shape is painted with the key colour in the position matching its quadrant (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), and the square is the output.

f931b4a8.rule: Split the input into four quadrants; the output has as many rows as TL has non-black cells and as many columns as TR has non-black cells, and is filled by tiling the smallest repeating tile of BR whose black cells are filled from BL, the copy of the tile at tile position (i, j) taking colour BL[i][j] with BL repeating.

faa9f03d.rule: Each coloured line is a damaged edge-to-edge path: its gaps and red cells are restored to its colour; at a corner beside a yellow cell the path is re-routed from that corner through the yellow cell straight to the grid edge and its old continuation beyond the corner is erased; wherever two paths cross, the same path lies on top at all their crossings, namely the one the input shows on top, except that the order is reversed for a pair in which one path carries red cells.

fc7cae8d.rule: A rectangle inside the grid has solid coloured edges on two adjacent sides, in the same two colours as two adjacent solid borders of the grid (the other two borders are grey noise); the output is the rectangle's interior, rotated or reflected so that each coloured edge faces the grid border of its colour.
